newsitem.title: ITALY: Seat falls in Milan on low bid reports.
newsitem.headline: Seat falls in Milan on low bid reports.

text.p: Italian yellow pages publishing company Seat SpA fell sharply on the Milan bourse on press reports that candidates in line to bid for the group had made much lower final offers than expected.
Seat was split off from state-controlled telecoms group Stet at the start of this year with the Treasury taking over state industrial holding IRI's stake of around 61 percent.

The Treasury has said due diligence would be completed by mid-April and Seat's sale carried out by mid-June. In February, ITT Corp said it was seeking along with other partners to acquire Seat. IRI is on record as saying it had received eight non-binding offers.

Daily La Repubblica said final offers by groups bidding for Seat were much lower than the Treasury had expected and that some of the candidates seemed to be having second thoughts. It said the withdrawal of U.S. grouping Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette merchant banking Europe capital partners was almost certain.
Italy's stock market council has estimated Seat's value at around 2.34 trillion lire.

"The possibility of lower than expected offers has put the stock under pressure," one dealer said. "Uncertainties about the relationship with Stet's telephone operating unit Telecom Italia, to which Seat's profitability is tightly linked, are also weighing."
At 1047 GMT, Seat shares were 4.92 percent lower at 547 lire on a generally firmer Milan bourse.
